cases.title: Mutual NDA
cases.source:
# Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement (SYNTHETIC)

This Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between
Northwind Materials GmbH ("Disclosing Party") and Cverbio Labs Inc.
("Receiving Party"). This document is fabricated for evaluation purposes and is
not a real agreement.

## 1. Definition of Confidential Information

Confidential Information means any and all information disclosed by either party
to the other, whether oral, written, or electronic, whether or not marked as
confidential.

## 2. Confidentiality Obligations

The Receiving Party shall keep all Confidential Information secret and shall not
disclose it to any third party without the prior written consent of the
Disclosing Party.

## 3. Term

This Agreement and the obligations of confidentiality set out herein shall
remain in effect in perpetuity.

## 4. Return or Destruction

Upon written request, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy all
Confidential Information in its possession within thirty (30) days.

## 5. Governing Law

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of
the Federal Republic of Germany.

## 6. Permitted Disclosures

The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information where disclosure is
required by law, court order, or a competent regulatory authority, provided that
the Receiving Party first obtains the prior written consent of the Disclosing
Party.

## 7. Residual Knowledge

Nothing in this Agreement restricts the Receiving Party from using ideas,
concepts, know-how, or techniques retained in the unaided memory of its personnel,
including for the benefit of third parties.

## 8. No Licence

Nothing in this Agreement grants the Receiving Party any licence or other right in
respect of the Disclosing Party's intellectual property.

## 9. Injunctive Relief

The parties acknowledge that damages may be an inadequate remedy for breach and
that the Disclosing Party may seek injunctive relief in addition to any other
remedy available at law.

## 10. Assignment

The Receiving Party may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any third
party, including a competitor of the disclosing counterparty, and no consent is
required for such an assignment.

## 11. Notices

Notices under this Agreement are effective when sent by email to the address
stated in the signature block.

gold.comment: Human-authored gold answer for the synthetic mutual NDA. severity_rationale records why each flag carries its severity, so the calibration can be challenged rather than assumed. Sections 8, 9 and 11 are deliberately unremarkable: a reviewer who flags them is producing false positives. clause_aliases declares synonyms for the SAME clause of the SAME document — spelling, plural and hyphenation variants, or an equally accurate name. Scoring a correct review as a miss because it wrote 'no_licence' for 'no_license' measures vocabulary, not legal judgment. An alias never maps onto a different clause.

review_context.objective: Pre-signature review before disclosing technical information to a prospective supplier.

severity_rationale.term: high — a perpetual confidentiality obligation with no survival period and no trade-secret carve-out is unenforceable in substance and unmanageable in practice; the receiving party cannot ever demonstrate compliance has ended.
severity_rationale.residual_knowledge: high — an unaided-memory residuals clause that permits use for the benefit of third parties defeats the operative obligation in section 2. Whatever a person remembers may be used for a competitor, so the agreement protects only documents, not information.
severity_rationale.permitted_disclosure: high — conditioning a legally compelled disclosure on the disclosing party's prior written consent is not capable of performance. The standard position is notice where lawful and cooperation in seeking protective relief, not consent.
severity_rationale.assignment: high — free assignment to a competitor of the disclosing party defeats the purpose of the agreement, since the counterparty can change to the one party the discloser would never have contracted with.
severity_rationale.definition: medium — a definition covering all information whether or not marked confidential is over-broad and lacks the standard public-domain, prior-possession and independent-development carve-outs. It is worse than market but negotiable.
severity_rationale.notices: low — email-only notice with no read receipt or deemed-delivery rule is slightly off-market and worth a note, not a blocker.

clauses.text: Defines Confidential Information broadly, including unmarked information.
Receiving Party must keep information secret and not disclose without consent.
Confidentiality obligations continue in perpetuity.
Return or destroy on request within 30 days.
Governed by the laws of Germany.
Legally compelled disclosure is permitted subject to prior written consent.
Unaided memory residuals may be used, including for third parties.
No licence granted in the disclosing party's intellectual property.
Injunctive relief available in addition to damages.
Receiving Party may assign to any third party without consent.
Notices effective when sent by email.
Receiving Party indemnifies the Disclosing Party for any breach.

risk_flags.rationale: A perpetual confidentiality term with no survival period is unenforceable in substance.
Unaided-memory residuals usable for third parties defeat the confidentiality obligation.
Definition covers unmarked information and lacks standard carve-outs.
Requiring consent before a compelled disclosure is unusual drafting.
Broad assignment rights are common in commercial agreements.

# Software-as-a-Service Agreement (SYNTHETIC)

This Software-as-a-Service Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between
Cverbio Labs Inc. ("Provider") and Northwind Materials GmbH ("Customer"). This
document is fabricated for evaluation purposes and is not a real agreement.

## 1. Service Levels

The Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% monthly
uptime, measured over each calendar month.

## 2. Data Protection

The Provider shall process Customer Personal Data only on documented instructions
from the Customer, in accordance with applicable data protection law.

## 3. Limitation of Liability

The Provider's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid
in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.

## 4. Term

The initial term of this Agreement is twelve (12) months from the effective date.

## 5. Auto-Renewal

This Agreement renews automatically for successive twelve (12) month terms unless
either party gives ninety (90) days written notice prior to the end of the
then-current term.

## 6. Sub-processors

The Provider may appoint sub-processors to process Customer Personal Data and
shall publish an updated list on its website. No notice to the Customer is
required.

## 7. Security

The Provider shall maintain industry standard security measures appropriate to a
provider of its size.

## 8. Intellectual Property and Service Improvement

The Customer grants the Provider a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence to
use Customer Data, including Customer Personal Data, to develop and train the
Provider's machine learning models and to create derivative products.

## 9. Indemnity

The Customer shall indemnify and hold harmless the Provider against all claims
arising from the use of the service, including claims that the service infringes
the intellectual property rights of a third party.

## 10. Fees

The Provider may increase the fees at any time on thirty (30) days written notice.
The Customer has no right to terminate on account of a fee increase.

## 11. Data Export on Termination

The Provider shall delete all Customer Data seven (7) days after termination. The
Customer may request an export within that period.

gold.comment: Human-authored gold answer for the synthetic SaaS agreement. severity_rationale records why each flag carries its severity. Service levels, data protection and term are deliberately clean: a reviewer who flags them is producing false positives. clause_aliases declares synonyms for the SAME clause of the SAME document — spelling, plural and hyphenation variants, or an equally accurate name. Scoring a correct review as a miss because it wrote 'no_licence' for 'no_license' measures vocabulary, not legal judgment. An alias never maps onto a different clause.

review_context.objective: Pre-signature review of a vendor paper contract for a business-critical system.

severity_rationale.auto_renewal: high — a ninety day notice window against a twelve month term means the decision point falls at month nine, and a single missed date commits the customer to another full year.
severity_rationale.ip_and_model_training: high — a perpetual irrevocable licence to train models on Customer Data expressly including Customer Personal Data has no lawful basis under the data protection clause in section 2, which limits processing to documented instructions. The two clauses contradict each other, and this one would make the provider a controller for that processing.
severity_rationale.indemnity: high — the customer indemnifying the provider against third-party claims that the provider's own service infringes reverses the normal allocation. The party that built the service and can clear the rights bears none of the risk.
severity_rationale.fees: high — an uncapped increase at any time on thirty days notice with no corresponding termination right is a unilateral right to reprice a locked-in customer.
severity_rationale.subprocessors: high — appointing sub-processors with website publication and no notice gives the customer no opportunity to object and does not meet Art. 28(2) GDPR, which the data protection clause purports to comply with.
severity_rationale.limitation_of_liability: medium — a twelve month fee cap is common market practice, but it carves out nothing for data breach, confidentiality or IP indemnity, which is worse than market and should be negotiated.
severity_rationale.security: medium — 'industry standard measures appropriate to a provider of its size' is unmeasurable and gives the customer nothing to audit against, but it is a drafting weakness rather than an absent obligation.
severity_rationale.data_export_on_termination: medium — a seven day deletion window with export only on request risks irreversible data loss on a missed deadline; thirty days with a standing export right is the ordinary position.

A defined deletion window is good data hygiene.

# Data Processing Agreement (SYNTHETIC)

This Data Processing Agreement ("DPA") is entered into between Northwind
Materials GmbH ("Controller") and Cverbio Analytics Inc. ("Processor") pursuant
to Article 28 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679. This document is fabricated for
evaluation purposes and is not a real agreement.

## 1. Subject Matter and Instructions

The Processor shall process personal data only on documented instructions from
the Controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third
country, unless required to do so by Union or Member State law to which the
Processor is subject.

## 2. Confidentiality

The Processor shall ensure that persons authorised to process the personal data
have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate
statutory obligation of confidentiality.

## 3. Security of Processing

The Processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures
to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, having regard to the
state of the art and the costs of implementation. A summary of such measures is
available on request.

## 4. Sub-processors

The Processor may engage sub-processors at its own discretion and shall inform
the Controller of any intended changes within a reasonable period after such
changes take effect. The Controller waives any right to object to the
appointment of a sub-processor.

## 5. Assistance with Data Subject Rights

Taking into account the nature of the processing, the Processor shall assist the
Controller by appropriate technical and organisational measures for the
fulfilment of the Controller's obligation to respond to requests for exercising
the data subject's rights laid down in Chapter III.

## 6. Personal Data Breaches and Impact Assessments

The Processor shall notify the Controller of a personal data breach within
fourteen (14) days of becoming aware of it, and shall provide reasonable
assistance with data protection impact assessments where commercially agreed.

## 7. Deletion and Return

Following termination of the services, the Processor may retain personal data
for its own legitimate business purposes, including product improvement and
model training, for an indefinite period.

## 8. Audits and Inspections

The Processor shall make available to the Controller a third-party audit
certificate once per calendar year. On-site inspections and audits by the
Controller or an auditor mandated by the Controller are expressly excluded.

## 9. International Transfers

The Processor may transfer personal data to its affiliates in third countries as
necessary for the provision of the services. The parties shall address any
required transfer mechanism separately if and when the need arises.

## 10. Governing Law

This DPA is governed by the laws of Germany.

gold.comment: Human-authored gold answer for the synthetic Art. 28 GDPR data processing agreement. Clause types follow Art. 28(3) lit. a to h in the regulation's own order, plus Chapter V transfers and governing law. severity_rationale records why each flag carries its severity, so the calibration can be challenged rather than assumed. clause_aliases declares synonyms for the SAME clause of the SAME document — spelling, plural and hyphenation variants, or an equally accurate name. Scoring a correct review as a miss because it wrote 'no_licence' for 'no_license' measures vocabulary, not legal judgment. An alias never maps onto a different clause.

review_context.objective: Art. 28 GDPR compliance review before appointing the processor.

severity_rationale.subprocessor_authorization: high — Art. 28(3)(d) and Art. 28(2) require the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation. The clause appoints sub-processors at the processor's discretion and has the controller waive its right to object, which removes the authorisation entirely rather than channelling it.
severity_rationale.deletion_return: high — Art. 28(3)(g) requires deletion or return at the controller's choice at the end of the services. Indefinite retention for the processor's own purposes, including model training, converts the processor into a controller for that processing without a lawful basis.
severity_rationale.audit_rights: high — Art. 28(3)(h) requires the processor to allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or a mandated auditor. Certification-first audit regimes are ordinary market practice and would be medium; this clause expressly excludes inspections, which removes a mandatory element rather than channelling it.
severity_rationale.international_transfers: high — Chapter V requires an adequacy decision or an Art. 46 safeguard to be in place before a transfer occurs. Permitting transfers now and addressing the mechanism 'if and when the need arises' inverts that sequence.
severity_rationale.breach_and_dpia_assistance: medium — Art. 28(3)(f) and Art. 33(2) require notification without undue delay. A fourteen day window is materially worse than the controller's own 72 hour obligation can absorb and should be negotiated, but a reviewer who accepted it with reasons would not be negligent.

risk_flags.rationale: Sub-processors appointed at the processor's discretion and the controller waives its right to object, which does not meet Art. 28(3)(d) GDPR.
Indefinite retention for the processor's own purposes after termination conflicts with Art. 28(3)(g) GDPR, which requires deletion or return at the controller's choice.
A fourteen day breach notification period is long relative to the controller's own 72 hour obligation.
An annual third-party certificate is a common market position.
Transfers are limited to affiliates for service provision.
